system_note: Audit of claim MR_06 (index stay) - summary and line-by-line reasoning with cited evidence: What was billed (selected, problem lines driving this determination): - Multiple, overlapping acute pancreatitis diagnoses were billed in principal position: K85.01 (idiopathic, POA=Y), K85.11 (biliary, uninfected necrosis, POA=Y), and K85.82 (infected necrosis, POA=Y). K57.21 (diverticulitis w/ perforation/abscess) and K65.0 (generalized peritonitis) were also billed. Sepsis lines: R65.21 (severe sepsis w/ septic shock, POA=Y), A41.50 (Gram-negative sepsis, POA=N) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella) were billed. Procedure lines include 0FBG3ZZ (excision of pancreas, percutaneous) among others. What the medical record actually documents (key citations): - The admission H&P and problem list document severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and explicitly list infected pancreatic necrosis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae (provider-attributed organism and source control procedures performed) (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658). Example: "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology." (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658) and the active problem list entry: "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae" (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658). - The discharge/transfer summary documents the infected necrosis with Klebsiella and the step-up interventions: "...infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem and a step-up approach including CT-guided percutaneous drainage on ICU day 13 followed by video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement on ICU day 16" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1079-1080). - Respiratory failure / ARDS and mechanical ventilation are well-documented with objective data: ABG/PF values and P/F ratio consistent with severe hypoxemia and invasive ventilation documented (Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, p. 242): "ABG (02:00): pH 7.31 / PaCO2 46 / PaO2 71 / HCO3 20; Lac 5.4; P/F 78." The Procedure Note documents endotracheal intubation (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Chart Notes, p. 520): "RSI with etomidate and rocuronium ... Device 8.0 ETT, 22 cm at teeth ... Placement confirmed clinically and radiographically." - Septic shock is documented in the hospital problem list and vasopressor use and elevated lactate are recorded (Hospital Problem List, p. 924: "Septic shock | R65.21 | 03/02/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10"). Physician orders show norepinephrine ordered and administered (Physician Orders, pp. 175-30): "Norepinephrine 0.1 mcg/kg/min IV via CVC - titrate to MAP >=65 mmHg | ... | Administered." Lactate values >2 are present on admission and subsequently (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658: "lactate 4.6 mmol/L"; Critical Care Progress Note, Chart Notes, p. 242: "Lac 5.4"). Policy requirements (select highlights): - Sepsis/septic shock (R65.21) validation requires provider documentation of septic shock and objective support (vasopressors + lactate >2 after resuscitation OR explicit provider documentation of septic shock). The record meets these requirements (Policy: Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, Validation Criteria: "Criterion 1 - Provider Documentation of Septic Shock" and vasopressor/lactate criteria). - When an organism is identified and documented as the cause of sepsis, the organism-specific sepsis code should be used (policy table: Klebsiella pneumoniae -> A41.53; "Additional Organism Code Needed?: No - organism embedded in code") (Policy: Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx, ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide). - Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia (J96.01) requires provider documentation of acute respiratory failure with hypoxia and objective evidence (ABG, low SpO2 on RA, P/F ratio) or initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation with attribution to respiratory failure; both are present (Policy: Acute Respiratory Failure with Hypoxia.docx, Validation Criteria). Auditor findings and corrective actions (reasoned line-by-line conclusions): 1) Conflicting / redundant pancreatitis coding (finding): the record documents severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with infected necrosis (provider statements and imaging). The simultaneous billing of K85.01 (idiopathic) and K85.11 (biliary with uninfected necrosis) alongside K85.82 (infected necrosis) is internally inconsistent and not supported. The chart explicitly documents gallstone etiology and infected necrosis, so: remove K85.01 and K85.11; retain K85.82 as principal diagnosis. Evidence: H&P imaging and active problem list (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658). 2) Sepsis organism specificity and redundant organism code (finding): the record documents Klebsiella pneumoniae causing infected pancreatic necrosis and sepsis; policy requires the organism-specific sepsis code (A41.53) when Klebsiella is identified. The claim billed A41.50 (Gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella as cause). Per policy, A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella) is the correct code and B96.1 is not additionally required when the A41.53 code is used. Action: replace A41.50 + B96.1 with A41.53. Evidence: H&P active problem list and Discharge Summary documenting "Klebsiella pneumoniae" and the sepsis policy selection guide (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 658; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1079-1080; Policy Documents/DRG/Sepsis and Septic Shock.docx). 3) R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) - supported as secondary diagnosis (no contest on severity tier) but sequencing: R65.21 should be coded concurrent with the appropriate A41.x organism sepsis code. The record documents septic shock (Hospital Problem List, p. 924), vasopressors administered (Physician Orders), and lactate >2 (History & Physical, Critical Care Progress Note), satisfying policy criteria. R65.21 remains but must be coded with the organism-specific A41.53 (not A41.50). Evidence: Hospital Problem List, Physician Orders, H&P and Progress Note lactate and vasopressor entries. 4) K57.21 (diverticulitis with perforation/abscess) and K65.0 (generalized peritonitis) - not supported by the clinical documentation retrieved. The problem lists, H&P, surgery consults, and discharge summary document infected pancreatic necrosis managed with percutaneous drainage and VARD; there is no provider documentation of diverticulitis with perforation/abscess or a diagnosis statement of generalized peritonitis in the record excerpts reviewed. Action: remove K57.21 and K65.0 from the billed diagnosis set. Evidence: absence of diverticulitis/peritonitis entries in the Hospital Problem List and Discharge Summary which enumerates discharge diagnoses but does not list diverticulitis or peritonitis (Hospital Problem List, p. 924; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, pp. 1079-1080). 5) Procedure coding: 0FBG3ZZ (Excision of pancreas, percutaneous approach) appears unsupported. The record documents percutaneous drainage and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD) and IR drainage, not a pancreatic resection/excision. Action: remove 0FBG3ZZ. Supported procedures include: 0BH17EZ (endotracheal tube insertion), 0DH64UZ (PEG/feeding device percutaneous), 0F9G30Z (drainage of pancreas, percutaneous), 02HV33Z (infusion device into SVC / central access / PICC/port context), 03HY32Z (arterial line / monitoring device), and 5A1D90Z (ventilation >96 consecutive hours) - those are supported by procedure notes, orders, and discharge summary (Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation, Physician Orders, Discharge / Transfer Summary). Corrected full claim-level lists (applies to entire index stay): - Revised diagnosis set (position 1 = principal): [ "K85.82", "K80.2", "R65.21", "A41.53", "J96.01", "J80", "N17.9", "I48.91", "E11.6", "K86.8", "I10", "E78.5", "K21.9" ] (Rationale: removed unsupported/contradictory K85.01 and K85.11; removed unsupported K57.21 and K65.0; replaced A41.50+B96.1 with A41.53 per organism-specific coding guidance; preserved other documented comorbidities.) - Revised procedure set (complete corrected ICD-10-PCS list): [ "0BH17EZ", "0DH64UZ", "0F9G30Z", "02HV33Z", "03HY32Z", "5A1D90Z" ] (Rationale: removed 0FBG3ZZ (excision) which is not supported; retained ETT, PEG, drainage, central access, arterial monitoring, and prolonged ventilation which are documented.) Disposition from record: transfer to long-term acute care for continued wound management, nutrition, and rehab (Transfer / Discharge Summary, Transfer Instructions, pp. 1076-1077; Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 1079-1080). Next steps / recommendation: apply the corrected diagnosis and procedure lists above for final coding/claim adjustment. Query the provider if coder/physician documentation is needed to certify the intended principal diagnosis sequencing (the record supports K85.82 as principal). Query if the coder needs physician attestation to change A41.50/B96.1 to A41.53 if the facility's coding policy requires clinician attestation for organism-specific sepsis codes. Audit performed using the retrieved chart excerpts and the referenced policy documents (citations below).
rationale_letter: Re: Audit Determination - Claim MR_06 Dear Provider/Coding Team, We completed a clinical audit of the hospital stay billed under claim MR_06 (admission 2026-03-02). The review compared the billed diagnosis and procedure codes to the treating clinician documentation and to the applicable coding policy rules. Our determination: Finding - coding adjustments are required because several billed diagnoses are unsupported or internally inconsistent with the clinical documentation, and the sepsis organism code is miscoded. Basis for Finding (specifics relied on): 1) Principal diagnosis and pancreatitis coding: The medical record documents severe necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis with infected pancreatic necrosis (CT imaging with 40-50% necrosis and explicit problem-list entries) rather than an idiopathic or uninfected necrotizing pancreatitis. The record therefore does not support K85.01 (idiopathic) or K85.11 (biliary with uninfected necrosis) together with an infected-necrosis code. Correct principal diagnosis: K85.82 - Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis (supported by the H&P and imaging). Evidence relied on: History & Physical (Admitting) (Chart Notes, p. 658): "Imaging confirmed severe necrotizing pancreatitis with 40-50% pancreatic necrosis and cholelithiasis as the presumptive etiology." and "2 | Infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae." 2) Sepsis organism specificity: The record identifies Klebsiella pneumoniae as the causative organism for the infected pancreatic necrosis and sepsis. Per the sepsis coding guidance, when Klebsiella is identified the organism-specific sepsis code A41.53 should be used. The claim instead contains A41.50 (Gram-negative sepsis, unspecified) plus B96.1 (Klebsiella as cause). Per policy, A41.53 (sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae) is the correct sepsis code and does not require an additional B96.1. Evidence relied on: Discharge / Transfer Summary (pp. 1079-1080): "...infected pancreatic necrosis with Klebsiella pneumoniae treated with meropenem..." and policy guidance (Sepsis and Septic Shock, ICD-10-CM Organism-Specific Sepsis Code Selection Guide). 3) Septic shock severity (R65.21): The record documents septic shock (provider problem list, vasopressor administration, and lactate >2), satisfying validation criteria for R65.21 as a secondary diagnosis; however, it must be paired with the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code (A41.53). Evidence: Hospital Problem List (p. 924): "Septic shock | R65.21 | 03/02/2026 | Resolved | Off vasopressors day 10"; Physician Orders (pp. 175-30): norepinephrine ordered and administered; and lactate values >2 recorded on admission and in ICU progress notes. 4) Unsupported/absent diagnoses: The chart does not substantiate diverticulitis with perforation and abscess (K57.21) or generalized peritonitis (K65.0). These codes should be removed unless supporting documentation not retrieved for this audit is provided. Evidence: Discharge and Problem List documentation enumerate the clinical course focused on pancreatic infected necrosis and do not document diverticulitis or generalized peritonitis (Hospital Problem List, p. 924; Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 1079-1080). 5) Procedure coding: The documentation supports percutaneous pancreatic drainage and video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (IR drainage and VARD) but does not support a pancreatic excision (0FBG3ZZ). Supported procedures include endotracheal intubation, PEG placement, percutaneous drainage of the pancreas, central venous / PICC access, arterial monitoring line placement, and prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hrs). Evidence: Discharge summary describing CT-guided percutaneous drainage and VARD (pp. 1079-1080); Procedure Note - Endotracheal Intubation (Chart Notes, p. 520); orders and procedure logs for PEG and drainage. Correction being made to the coded claim (complete corrected sets): - Revised diagnosis set (position 1 = principal): ["K85.82", "K80.2", "R65.21", "A41.53", "J96.01", "J80", "N17.9", "I48.91", "E11.6", "K86.8", "I10", "E78.5", "K21.9"]. - Revised procedure set: ["0BH17EZ", "0DH64UZ", "0F9G30Z", "02HV33Z", "03HY32Z", "5A1D90Z"]. If you disagree with these changes, please submit supporting clinician documentation (provider notes or attestation) that specifically documents any of the following: - a documented principal diagnosis other than infected necrotizing pancreatitis that occasioned the admission; or - provider-validated evidence of diverticulitis with perforation and/or generalized peritonitis; or - clinician attestation that A41.50 (with B96.1) rather than A41.53 is the intended sepsis coding (with rationale). Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team
